amendments.because: The owner asked on 2026-10-01 to fix it for good: cover every common install folder and have doctor catch any machine where hooks still can't find forge
amendments.done_when: The host hook commands forge sync writes for Codex and Claude Code find forge even when the hook's PATH lacks uv's tool folder: they add uv's default tool bin folder (XDG_BIN_HOME, else HOME/.local/bin) to the front of PATH before running forge, and still block (exit 2) when forge can't be found at all. A command-level test runs each synced hook command with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and a HOME whose .local/bin holds forge, and it runs; another with no forge anywhere still blocks. Forge's own repo's hook files are regenerated.

amendments.because: The owner hit this on a fresh machine on 2026-10-01: with no forge installed, Forge's own hooks blocked every command, including the ones needed to install it; fix it for good
amendments.done_when: The host hook commands forge sync writes for Codex and Claude Code find forge even when the hook's PATH lacks its install folder: before running forge they put UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR, XDG_BIN_HOME, HOME/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin (those that are set) in front of PATH, and still block (exit 2) when forge can't be found at all. forge doctor runs each synced hook command with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and reports, with the fix to apply, any that can't find forge. Command-level tests: each synced hook runs with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and forge under HOME/.local/bin, and under a UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR folder; with no forge anywhere it still blocks; doctor reports a hook that can't find forge. Forge's own repo's hook files are regenerated.

done_when: The host hook commands forge sync writes for Codex and Claude Code never leave a machine blocked just because forge isn't on the hook's PATH. In order they: run forge from PATH after putting UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR, XDG_BIN_HOME, HOME/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin (those that exist) in front; else, in Forge's own repo (repo = forge-source), run the checkout's code through uv; else, when uv is available, run the repo's pinned release through uvx (git+https://github.com/knacklabs/symphony-forge@<pinned version>); else block (exit 2) with one plain line naming the install command for the pinned release and forge doctor, never a bare 'command not found'. forge doctor runs each synced hook command with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and reports any that can't run. Command-level tests: forge under HOME/.local/bin and under UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin; no forge but uv present (runs the pinned release; uvx stubbed at its edge); Forge's own repo with no forge installed; nothing available (blocks with the plain line); doctor reporting a hook that can't run. Forge's own repo's hook files are regenerated.
why: Codex runs its hooks with a PATH that lacks the folder uv installs forge into, so every hook command fails with 'forge: command not found' and the fail-closed deny hook blocks every shell command, even pwd, for a Codex orchestrator
